detail.title: State Dependency and Persistence in Autocatalytic Reaction Networks
detail.summary: Autocatalytic networks exhibit hysteresis and compositional stability that can mimic memory. The analysis distinguishes between simple thermodynamic relaxation times and functional memory storage, noting that sustained historical influence requires non-linear coupling to growth-regimes.
detail.reason: Synthesis of existing theoretical frameworks regarding memory in non-equilbrium reaction networks.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Autocatalytic Memory
detail.question: Can autocatalytic reaction networks retain history-dependent states that influence future system behavior, independent of templated copying?
